subject: Urgent: Brightbeam API EU latency surge and resolution offer
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@brightbeam.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Large spike in EU p95/p99 since 08:45 UTC — urgent

Hi Marissa / Rishi,

We started seeing a sharp increase in response times from Redwood’s hosted API for requests originating in our EU region at ~08:45 UTC. P95 has jumped from ~120ms to ~1.1s and p99 is >2.5s. Several of our production customer-facing queries are timing out.

What we observed:
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat.
- Impact window: 08:45 UTC -> ongoing as of this email.
- Sample metrics attached (latency-spike-20270402-dashboard.png).
- Trace headers included in the attached trace-headers-logs-20270402.txt.

This is causing customer-visible errors and one-seat alerts in our incident channel. Can you confirm receipt and an ETA for a mitigation? We can open a bridge if helpful.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Ops Lead, Brightbeam Analytics
ops@brightbeam.ai

Attachment: latency-spike-20270402-dashboard.png
Attachment: trace-headers-logs-20270402.txt

Hi Lena — thanks for the alert and for the attachments. We're on it.

Immediate next steps:

I'll keep you updated every 30–45 minutes. If you prefer a call, say the word and I’ll share a bridge link.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: URGENT: Brightbeam EU latency spike — triage requested

Team — Brightbeam (DB-7894) reports sustained p95/p99 spikes affecting production customers in EU. Marissa has acknowledged and shared dashboards/logs.

Customer severity: P1 for them (customer-impacting timeouts). Requesting immediate triage and an initial hypothesis within 30 minutes.

Useful context and asks:
- Attachments from customer include trace headers and a snapshot of Datadog graphs.
- Please check routing policies, egress mappings, and any recent policy rollouts tied to region selection (last change window: 02 Apr 04:00 UTC).
- If this is routing-related, identify rollback path and quick mitigations (route pinning, region routing override).

I’ll keep Marissa and Brightbeam updated; escalate to leadership if we need exec comms.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 14:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: Brightbeam EU latency spike — initial triage

Quick update from SRE triage:
- Root cause (initial): a routing-policy change pushed at 04:00 UTC modified egress mapping for the EU zone. Traffic for certain EU ingress points began being routed through our us-west egress pool due to an inverted match in the new policy.
- Effect: additional cross-region RTT (~600–900ms) causing the observed p95/p99 jumps. Error rates increased slightly where client-side timeouts occurred.

Evidence and artifacts:
- Sample traces show EU client IP -> us-west host -> model shard (in us-west) before returning to EU.
- Attached logs: trace-headers-logs-20270402.txt and selected host-level traces.
- Datadog link (internal): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/abc-123/eu-api-latency (redwood internal view).

Immediate mitigation applied (10:20 UTC):
- Rolled back the policy change that introduced the inverted match.
- Applied a temporary routing override to pin Brightbeam EU traffic to EU egress.

Current status: latency is trending down but still above baseline for some tail percentiles; monitoring is in place. We recommend keeping the override until we validate traffic is fully back to normal for 24 hours.

Next steps:
- Engineering will run a focused audit of the policy grammar and add unit tests to prevent inverted-match regressions.
- Ops to run a canary for policy changes with explicit regional traffic tests.

– Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: trace-headers-logs-20270402.txt

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 11:18:00 +0000
Subject: Internal summary and remediation plan — Brightbeam EU incident

Team — summary for execs and customer communication:

What happened:
- A routing policy change introduced an inverted match on region tags; EU traffic for some ingress points was incorrectly matched and egressed via us-west. This added cross-region RTT and produced the observed p95/p99 regression.

What we did quickly:
- Rolled back the offending policy at 10:20 UTC on 02 Apr.
- Applied a routing override to pin Brightbeam EU traffic to EU egress.
- Began heightened monitoring and trace collection.

Planned follow-ups:
- Deploy grammar-level unit tests for routing policies (INF-4521).
- Add automated regional e2e checks to the policy rollout pipeline.
- Prepare a customer postmortem and propose a short-term billing adjustment (suggested: 10% invoice credit for the affected window).

Recommended comms:
- Customer-facing note acknowledging the incident, root cause, steps taken, and remediation timeline. Offer SLA credit and invite them to a postmortem call.

I will coordinate the postmortem write-up and share a draft by EOD Monday. If we escalate financial exceptions beyond the standard credit, let me know and I’ll loop finance/legal.

Sergio Alvarez
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: sla-summary-bb.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@brightbeam.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 18:22:00 +0000
Subject: Resolved: Brightbeam EU latency surge — summary and next steps

Hi Lena — thanks again for your patience while we investigated.

Summary of resolution:
- Root cause: a recently deployed routing-policy rule inadvertently matched EU traffic to a us-west egress pool (inverted match).
- What we did: rolled back the change immediately (10:20 UTC on 02 Apr) and applied a regional override to ensure EU traffic remains in-region while we validate.
- Status: tail latency (p95/p99) has returned to within acceptable variance for the last 6 hours; we will keep the override for 24 hours of stable telemetry.

Customer impact & remediation offer:
- We recognize the incident caused customer-visible errors and delays. Redwood is offering a 10% credit for the invoice covering the affected window (02 Apr 08:45–11:30 UTC). If you prefer a different accommodation, we are open to discuss.

Next steps and invites:
- We will share a technical postmortem (draft by Monday) that includes root cause, timeline, and preventive actions.
- Would Brightbeam like a live postmortem call this week? We can set up a joint session with SRE and infra.

If you want a bridge or additional logs, I can share immediately. Apologies for the disruption — we appreciate the partnership and will improve our rollout safeguards.

Warmly,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
